title: Primary 4 Adding and Subtracting Decimals

standard_text: Adding and subtracting decimals (up to 2 decimal places)
meta_desc: Free P4 maths: add and subtract decimals up to 2 decimal places, estimate to check, and solve money and measurement problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the decimal points, then add or subtract like whole numbers.
body_html:
The idea: line up the decimal points

Add and subtract decimals the same way as whole numbers, but first line up the decimal points. Then ones are under ones, tenths under tenths and hundredths under hundredths. You can only add or subtract digits in the same place.

Different numbers of decimal places

Write a zero so both numbers have the same number of decimal places. A zero at the end does not change the value: 3.5 = 3.50.

Rename like whole numbers

10 hundredths = 1 tenth and 10 tenths = 1 one. When a column makes 10 or more, rename. The 1 can cross the decimal point.

Subtract from a whole number

To take a decimal from a whole number, give the whole number a decimal point and zeros: 10 = 10.00. When you rename across zeros, each 0 becomes 9 and the place you need gets 10.

Example 1

What is 5.03 − 1.26?

Hundredths: 3 − 6 needs renaming, but the tenths digit is 0. Rename 1 one: 4 ones, 9 tenths, 13 hundredths. 13 − 6 = 7, 9 − 2 = 7, 4 − 1 = 3. Check: 3.77 + 1.26 = 5.03.

Answer: 3.77

Estimate first, then check

Round each number to the nearest whole number and do the easy calculation. 3.5 + 1.25 is about 4 + 1 = 5, so 4.75 makes sense and 1.6 does not. Check a subtraction by adding back: 6.55 + 3.45 = 10.

Word problems: draw a bar model

Draw the whole and the parts. Write money in dollars with 2 decimal places (85¢ = $0.85). Use the same unit for every number.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Lining up the last digits (3.5 + 1.25 = 1.6)Line up the decimal points. Write 3.5 as 3.50
Writing 11 tenths as 0.11 (0.6 + 0.5 = 0.11)Rename 10 tenths as 1 one: 0.6 + 0.5 = 1.1
Not writing the zeros (10 − 3.45 = 7.45)Write 10 as 10.00, then rename to subtract
Forgetting the 1 that crosses the point (3.78 + 2.54 = 5.32)10 tenths = 1 one. Add the 1 to the ones
Dropping the decimal point (3.5 + 1.25 = 475)Bring the point straight down into the answer

faq.q: What is taught in P4 adding and subtracting decimals?
faq.a: In Primary 4, students add and subtract decimals up to 2 decimal places, such as 3.5 + 1.25 and 10 − 3.45. They estimate to check their answers and solve word problems with money and measurements.

faq.q: How do I explain adding decimals like 3.5 + 1.25 to my child?
faq.a: Line up the decimal points and write 3.5 as 3.50, so every digit has a partner in the same place. Then add from the right like whole numbers: 3.50 + 1.25 = 4.75.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when adding decimals?
faq.a: The most common mistake is lining up the last digits instead of the decimal points, so 3.5 + 1.25 becomes 1.6. Another is writing 0.6 + 0.5 = 0.11: 6 tenths + 5 tenths = 11 tenths = 1.1.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Adding and subtracting decimals up to 2 decimal places is part of the Primary 4 Decimals topic in the MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus (Standard Mathematics).

items.q: You add 4.36 + 2.5 in columns with the decimal points lined up. Which digit of 2.5 goes under the 3?
items.e: The 3 in 4.36 is in the tenths place. Line up the decimal points and tenths sit under tenths: the tenths digit of 2.5 is 5. The 2 is in the ones place, so it goes under the 4.

items.q: In 37.26 − 5.8, the digits are lined up by place value. Which digit of 37.26 is above the 5?
items.e: 5 is the ones digit of 5.8. The ones digit of 37.26 is 7, so the 5 goes under the 7. The 3 is in the tens place and has no digit under it.

items.q: Hafiz says 0.6 + 0.5 = 0.11. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 6 tenths + 5 tenths = 11 tenths. Rename 10 tenths as 1 one, so 11 tenths = 1 one and 1 tenth = 1.1. 0.11 is only 11 hundredths, which is less than 0.6 alone.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 4 + 3 = 7. Ones: 5 + 8 = 13, write 13. Answer: 13.7. Check: 13.7 − 8.3 = 5.4.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 7 + 2 = 9. Tenths: 1 + 4 = 5. Ones: 2 + 1 = 3. Answer: 3.59. Check: 3.59 − 1.42 = 2.17.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 5 − 9 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 15 − 9 = 6. Ones: 6 − 5 = 1. Answer: 1.6. Check: 1.6 + 5.9 = 7.5.

items.q: What is 0.5 + 0.9?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 5 + 9 = 14, write 4 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 0 + 0 + 1 = 1. Answer: 1.4. Check: 1.4 − 0.9 = 0.5.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 2 − 3 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 12 − 3 = 9. Ones: 5 − 5 = 0. Tens: bring down 2. Answer: 20.9. Check: 20.9 + 5.3 = 26.2.

items.q: What is 4.4 + 6.7?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 4 + 7 = 11, write 1 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 4 + 6 + 1 = 11, write 11. Answer: 11.1. Check: 11.1 − 6.7 = 4.4.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 + 9 = 11, write 1 and rename 10 hundredths as 1 tenth. Tenths: 6 + 3 + 1 = 10, write 0 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 1 + 3 + 1 = 5. Answer: 5.01. Check: 5.01 − 3.39 = 1.62.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 8 needs renaming. Rename 1 tenth as 10 hundredths: 12 − 8 = 4. Tenths: 8 − 0 = 8. Ones: 6 − 1 = 5. Answer: 5.84. Check: 5.84 + 1.08 = 6.92.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 5 + 5 + 1 = 11, write 1 and rename 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 5 + 1 = 6. Answer: 61.3. Check: 61.3 − 55.5 = 5.8.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 9 − 3 = 6. Tenths: 9 − 2 = 7. Ones: 1 − 9 needs renaming. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 11 − 9 = 2. Tens: bring down 6. Answer: 62.76. Check: 62.76 + 9.23 = 71.99.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 4 + 8 = 12, write 2 and rename 10 hundredths as 1 tenth. Tenths: 6 + 3 + 1 = 10, write 0 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 0 + 0 + 1 = 1. Answer: 1.02. Check: 1.02 − 0.38 = 0.64.
Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 3 − 6 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 13 − 6 = 7. Ones: 8 − 1 = 7. Tens: 7 − 7 = 0. Answer: 7.7. Check: 7.7 + 71.6 = 79.3.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 7 + 1 = 8. Tenths: 2 + 8 = 10, write 0 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 8 + 1 + 1 = 10, write 0 and rename 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 7 + 8 + 1 = 16, write 16. Answer: 160.08. Check: 160.08 − 81.81 = 78.27.

Ones: 5 − 6 needs renaming. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 15 − 6 = 9. Tens: 5 − 1 = 4. Answer: 49.53. Check: 49.53 + 16.98 = 66.51.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 + 2 = 4. Tenths: 3 + 7 = 10, write 0 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 6 + 5 + 1 = 12, write 2 and rename 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 5 + 1 = 6. Answer: 62.04. Check: 62.04 − 5.72 = 56.32.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 1 − 4 needs renaming. Rename 1 tenth as 10 hundredths: 11 − 4 = 7. Tenths: 2 − 6 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 12 − 6 = 6. Answer: 0.67. Check: 0.67 + 0.64 = 1.31.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 6 + 6 = 12, write 2 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 8 + 0 + 1 = 9. Tens: 2 + 2 = 4. Answer: 49.2. Check: 49.2 − 20.6 = 28.6.

items.q: To add 3.5 + 1.25, you write 3.5 with two decimal places. Which number is equal to 3.5?
items.e: A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 3.5 = 3 ones and 5 tenths = 3.50. 3.05 is wrong: it moves the 5 to the hundredths place.

items.q: What is 3.5 + 1.25?
items.e: Line up the decimal points and write 3.5 as 3.50. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 5 + 2 = 7. Ones: 3 + 1 = 4. Answer: 4.75. 1.6 comes from lining up the last digits (35 + 125 = 160). 475 drops the decimal point.

items.q: Devi lined up the last digits and got 2.69. What is the correct sum?
items.e: Line up the decimal points, not the last digits: 5.60 + 2.13. Hundredths: 0 + 3 = 3. Tenths: 6 + 1 = 7. Ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Answer: 7.73. Estimate: 6 + 2 = 8, so 2.69 is far too small.

items.q: To find 9 + 3.47, you can write 9 with a decimal point. Which number is equal to 9?
items.e: A whole number has its decimal point after the ones digit, so 9 = 9.00. Then the 9 ones sit over the 3 ones: 9.00 + 3.47 = 12.47.

items.q: Raju lined up the last digits and got 4.43. What is the correct sum?
items.e: 18 is a whole number, so its point is after the 8: 18 = 18.00 (not 1.8). Line up the points: 18.00 + 4.25. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 0 + 2 = 2. Ones: 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 and rename 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 22.25.

items.q: What is 0.7 + 0.46?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 0.7 as 0.70. Hundredths: 0 + 6 = 6. Tenths: 7 + 4 = 11, write 1 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 0 + 0 + 1 = 1. Answer: 1.16. Check: 1.16 − 0.46 = 0.7.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 4.8 as 4.80. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 3 + 8 = 11, write 1 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 2 + 4 + 1 = 7. Answer: 7.15. Check: 7.15 − 4.8 = 2.35.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 4.5 as 4.50. Hundredths: 4 + 0 = 4. Tenths: 4 + 5 = 9. Ones: 5 + 4 = 9. Answer: 9.94. Check: 9.94 − 4.5 = 5.44.

items.q: What is 5.48 + 0.6?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 0.6 as 0.60. Hundredths: 8 + 0 = 8. Tenths: 4 + 6 = 10, write 0 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 5 + 0 + 1 = 6. Answer: 6.08. Check: 6.08 − 0.6 = 5.48.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 90.8 as 90.80. Hundredths: 0 + 1 = 1. Tenths: 8 + 3 = 11, write 1 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 0 + 5 + 1 = 6. Tens: bring down 9. Answer: 96.11. Check: 96.11 − 5.31 = 90.8.

items.q: What is 8.09 − 6.8?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 6.8 as 6.80. Hundredths: 9 − 0 = 9. Tenths: 0 − 8 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 10 − 8 = 2. Ones: 7 − 6 = 1. Answer: 1.29. Check: 1.29 + 6.8 = 8.09.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 7 as 7.00. Hundredths: 0 + 9 = 9. Tenths: 0 + 4 = 4. Ones: 7 + 3 = 10, write 10. Answer: 10.49. Check: 10.49 − 3.49 = 7.

Line up the decimal points. Write 8.1 as 8.10. Hundredths: 5 − 0 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 1 = 8. Ones: 0 − 8 needs renaming. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 10 − 8 = 2. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 12.85. Check: 12.85 + 8.1 = 20.95.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 9.7 as 9.70. Hundredths: 1 + 0 = 1. Tenths: 1 + 7 = 8. Ones: 1 + 9 = 10, write 0 and rename 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 9 + 1 = 10, write 10. Answer: 100.81. Check: 100.81 − 9.7 = 91.11.

items.q: What is 3.5 − 0.01?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 3.5 as 3.50. Hundredths: 0 − 1 needs renaming. Rename 1 tenth as 10 hundredths: 10 − 1 = 9. Tenths: 4 − 0 = 4. Ones: bring down 3. Answer: 3.49. Check: 3.49 + 0.01 = 3.5.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 9.7 as 9.70. Hundredths: 7 + 0 = 7. Tenths: 9 + 7 = 16, write 6 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 0 + 9 + 1 = 10, write 10. Answer: 10.67. Check: 10.67 − 9.7 = 0.97.

Line up the decimal points. Write 43.3 as 43.30. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming. Rename 1 tenth as 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 2 − 7 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 12 − 7 = 5. Ones: 2 − 3 needs renaming. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 12 − 3 = 9. Tens: bring down 3. Answer: 39.55. Check: 39.55 + 3.75 = 43.3.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 73.8 as 73.80. Hundredths: 0 + 4 = 4. Tenths: 8 + 3 = 11, write 1 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 3 + 6 + 1 = 10, write 0 and rename 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 7 + 7 + 1 = 15, write 15. Answer: 150.14. Check: 150.14 − 76.34 = 73.8.

items.q: What is 41.36 − 8?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 8 as 8.00. Hundredths: 6 − 0 = 6. Tenths: 3 − 0 = 3. Ones: 1 − 8 needs renaming. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 11 − 8 = 3. Tens: bring down 3. Answer: 33.36. Check: 33.36 + 8 = 41.36.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 5 as 5.0. Tenths: 8 + 0 = 8. Ones: 1 + 5 = 6. Tens: bring down 9. Answer: 96.8. Check: 96.8 − 5 = 91.8.

sets.title: Subtract with renaming and from whole numbers

items.q: To find 7 − 2.35, how should you write 7 so both numbers have hundredths?
items.e: 7 is 7 ones, and its decimal point is after the 7. Write 7.00: the two zeros hold the tenths and hundredths places. Then 7.00 − 2.35 = 4.65.

items.q: Zhi Hao found 7 − 2.35 = 4.65. Which addition checks his answer?
items.e: Addition undoes subtraction. Add the answer to the number taken away: 4.65 + 2.35 = 7.00 = 7. You get back the starting number, so his answer is right.

items.q: Ethan says 10 − 3.45 = 7.45. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Ethan did not write the zeros: 10 − 3 = 7, then brought down .45. Write 10 as 10.00 and rename 1 ten: 0 tens, 9 ones, 9 tenths and 10 hundredths. 10 − 5 = 5, 9 − 4 = 5, 9 − 3 = 6. Answer: 6.55. Check: 6.55 + 3.45 = 10. 7.55 forgets to take 1 from the 10 when renaming. 13.45 adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 8 needs renaming. Rename 1 tenth as 10 hundredths: 12 − 8 = 4. Tenths: 2 − 5 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 12 − 5 = 7. Ones: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 4.74. Check: 4.74 + 2.58 = 7.32.

items.q: What is 8.4 − 3.7?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 4 − 7 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 14 − 7 = 7. Ones: 7 − 3 = 4. Answer: 4.7. Check: 4.7 + 3.7 = 8.4.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 2.9 as 2.90. Hundredths: 6 − 0 = 6. Tenths: 1 − 9 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 11 − 9 = 2. Ones: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 2.26. Check: 2.26 + 2.9 = 5.16.

Line up the decimal points. Write 12.5 as 12.50. Hundredths: 0 − 3 needs renaming. Rename 1 tenth as 10 hundredths: 10 − 3 = 7. Tenths: 4 − 8 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 14 − 8 = 6. Ones: 1 − 4 needs renaming. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 11 − 4 = 7. Answer: 7.67. Check: 7.67 + 4.83 = 12.5.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 5 as 5.00. Hundredths: 0 − 7 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 one: the ones become 4, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 7 = 3. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 2.63. Check: 2.63 + 2.37 = 5.

items.q: What is 1 − 0.35?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 1 as 1.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 one: the ones become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Answer: 0.65. Check: 0.65 + 0.35 = 1.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 20 as 20.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 ten: the tens become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 7 = 2. Ones: 9 − 6 = 3. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 13.25. Check: 13.25 + 6.75 = 20.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 5 − 7 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 one: the ones become 3, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 15. 15 − 7 = 8. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 3 − 1 = 2. Answer: 2.68. Check: 2.68 + 1.37 = 4.05.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 6 as 6.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 one: the ones become 5, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 2 = 7. Ones: bring down 5. Answer: 5.75. Check: 5.75 + 0.25 = 6.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 4 − 7 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 ten: the tens become 2, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 14. 14 − 7 = 7. Tenths: 9 − 6 = 3. Ones: 9 − 2 = 7. Tens: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 17.37. Check: 17.37 + 12.67 = 30.04.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 3 as 3.0. Tenths: 0 − 4 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 10 − 4 = 6. Ones: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 1.6. Check: 1.6 + 1.4 = 3.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 5 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 one: the ones become 7, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 12. 12 − 5 = 7. Tenths: 9 − 0 = 9. Ones: 7 − 3 = 4. Answer: 4.97. Check: 4.97 + 3.05 = 8.02.

items.q: What is 8 − 4.55?

Rename 1 one: the ones become 5, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 9 = 1. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 5 − 4 = 1. Tens: bring down 6. Answer: 61.61. Check: 61.61 + 4.39 = 66.

items.q: What is 70 − 43.7?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 70 as 70.0. Tenths: 0 − 7 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 ten: the tens become 6, each 0 becomes 9, and the tenths become 10. 10 − 7 = 3. Ones: 9 − 3 = 6. Tens: 6 − 4 = 2. Answer: 26.3. Check: 26.3 + 43.7 = 70.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 7 as 7.00. Hundredths: 0 − 7 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 one: the ones become 6, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 7 = 3. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: bring down 6. Answer: 6.63. Check: 6.63 + 0.37 = 7.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest whole number. Which is the best estimate for 6.82 + 3.29?
items.e: 6.82 rounds to 7 and 3.29 rounds to 3. 7 + 3 = 10. The exact answer, 10.11, is close to 10.

items.q: Nurul worked out 5.6 + 2.13 and got 2.69. Use an estimate to check. What does the estimate show?

items.e: 5.6 rounds to 6 and 2.13 rounds to 2, so the answer should be about 6 + 2 = 8. 2.69 is much smaller than 8, so it is too small. Nurul probably lined up the last digits instead of the decimal points. The correct answer is 7.73.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 9.45 + 12.7
items.e: 9.45 + 12.7 is about 9 + 13 = 22. Only 22.15 is close to 22. Check by working it out: Write 12.7 as 12.70. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 4 + 7 = 11, write 1 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 9 + 2 + 1 = 12, write 2 and rename 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 22.15. Check: 22.15 − 12.7 = 9.45.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 40 − 18.35
items.e: 40 − 18.35 is about 40 − 18 = 22. Only 21.65 is close to 22. Check by working it out: Write 40 as 40.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 ten: the tens become 3, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 9 − 8 = 1. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. Answer: 21.65. Check: 21.65 + 18.35 = 40.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 6.07 + 2.9
items.e: 6.07 + 2.9 is about 6 + 3 = 9. Only 8.97 is close to 9. Check by working it out: Write 2.9 as 2.90. Hundredths: 7 + 0 = 7. Tenths: 0 + 9 = 9. Ones: 6 + 2 = 8. Answer: 8.97. Check: 8.97 − 2.9 = 6.07.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 13.4 − 5.85
items.e: 13.4 − 5.85 is about 13 − 6 = 7. Only 7.55 is close to 7. Check by working it out: Write 13.4 as 13.40. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming. Rename 1 tenth as 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 3 − 8 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 13 − 8 = 5. Ones: 2 − 5 needs renaming. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 12 − 5 = 7. Answer: 7.55. Check: 7.55 + 5.85 = 13.4.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 0.85 + 2.6
items.e: 0.85 + 2.6 is about 1 + 3 = 4. Only 3.45 is close to 4. Check by working it out: Write 2.6 as 2.60. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 8 + 6 = 14, write 4 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 0 + 2 + 1 = 3. Answer: 3.45. Check: 3.45 − 2.6 = 0.85.

items.q: At the hawker centre, Arjun buys a plate of chicken rice for $4.50 and a cup of lime juice for $1.80. How much does he spend?
items.e: Put the two prices together: add. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 0 + 0 = 0. Tenths: 5 + 8 = 13, write 3 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 4 + 1 + 1 = 6. Answer: $6.30. Check: $6.30 − $1.80 = $4.50.

items.q: Wei Ming pays for a $13.45 storybook with a $20 note. How much change does he get?
items.e: Change is what is left: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 20 as 20.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 ten: the tens become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 4 = 5. Ones: 9 − 3 = 6. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: $6.55. Check: $6.55 + $13.45 = $20.00.

items.q: Hui Min buys a pencil for 85¢ and a ruler for $1.40 at the school bookshop. How much does she pay?
items.e: Write the cents in dollars first: 85¢ = $0.85. $0.85 + $1.40: hundredths 5 + 0 = 5, tenths 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one, ones 0 + 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: $2.25. $86.40 adds 85 dollars. $9.90 uses 85¢ = $8.50. $1.25 forgets the renamed 1 one.

items.q: Sarah’s EZ-Link card has $12.40 on it. After a bus ride to the Singapore Zoo, it has $11.25 left. How much was the bus fare?
items.e: The fare is the difference between the two amounts: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming. Rename 1 tenth as 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 3 − 2 = 1. Ones: 2 − 1 = 1. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: $1.15. Check: $1.15 + $11.25 = $12.40.

items.q: Kumar’s mother buys 1.35 kg of rambutans and 0.9 kg of mangosteens at the market. What is the total mass of the fruit?
items.e: Total means add. Line up the decimal points. Write 0.9 as 0.90. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 3 + 9 = 12, write 2 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 1 + 0 + 1 = 2. Answer: 2.25 kg. Check: 2.25 − 0.9 = 1.35.

items.q: Mrs Lim has a ribbon 4 m long. She cuts off 1.35 m to wrap a present for Children’s Day. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Take the part cut off away: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 4 as 4.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming, but the next place is 0. Rename 1 one: the ones become 3, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 3 − 1 = 2. Answer: 2.65 m. Check: 2.65 + 1.35 = 4.

items.q: Kavya’s water bottle has 1.5 ℓ of water. She drinks 0.65 ℓ during the CCA session. How much water is left?
items.e: Take away what she drank: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 1.5 as 1.50. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming. Rename 1 tenth as 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 − 6 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 14 − 6 = 8. Answer: 0.85 ℓ. Check: 0.85 + 0.65 = 1.5.

items.q: On Sports Day, Priya ran 100 m in 16.25 s and Farah ran it in 15.8 s. How many seconds faster was Farah?
items.e: The faster runner has the smaller time. Find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 15.8 as 15.80. Hundredths: 5 − 0 = 5. Tenths: 2 − 8 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 12 − 8 = 4. Ones: 5 − 5 = 0. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 0.45 s. Check: 0.45 + 15.8 = 16.25.

items.q: In the long jump, Jun Jie jumps 2.45 m. Mei Ling jumps 0.38 m farther than Jun Jie. How far does Mei Ling jump?
items.e: Mei Ling’s bar is Jun Jie’s bar and 0.38 m more, so add: 2.45 + 0.38. Hundredths: 5 + 8 = 13, write 3 and rename 10 hundredths as 1 tenth. Tenths: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. Ones: 2. Answer: 2.83 m. 2.07 m subtracts instead of adding. 2.73 m forgets the renamed 1 tenth.

items.q: Hafiz’s family has breakfast at a coffee shop. A kaya toast set costs $3.80 and a plate of prata costs $5.50. What is the total cost?
items.e: Total cost means add. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 0 + 0 = 0. Tenths: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 3 + 5 + 1 = 9. Answer: $9.30. Check: $9.30 − $5.50 = $3.80.

items.q: Devi has $20. She buys a cup of bubble tea for $4.60 and a book for $7.85. How much money does she have left?
items.e: Step 1, money spent: $4.60 + $7.85 = $12.45. Step 2, money left: $20.00 − $12.45 = $7.55. Check: $7.55 + $12.45 = $20. $12.45 is the money spent, not left. $8.45 forgets to write $20 as $20.00. $15.40 takes away only the bubble tea.

items.q: At Gardens by the Bay, Raju’s class walks 2.6 km in the morning and 1.75 km in the afternoon. How far do they walk altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Line up the decimal points. Write 2.6 as 2.60. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 7 = 13, write 3 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Answer: 4.35 km. Check: 4.35 − 1.75 = 2.6.

items.q: Mdm Wong has 2.4 ℓ of soup in a pot. She adds 0.85 ℓ of water. How much liquid is in the pot now?
items.e: Put the two amounts together: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 2.4 as 2.40. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 + 8 = 12, write 2 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 2 + 0 + 1 = 3. Answer: 3.25 ℓ. Check: 3.25 − 0.85 = 2.4.

items.q: A durian has a mass of 2.15 kg. A pineapple has a mass of 1.6 kg. How much heavier is the durian?
items.e: How much heavier means find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 1.6 as 1.60. Hundredths: 5 − 0 = 5. Tenths: 1 − 6 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 11 − 6 = 5. Ones: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 0.55 kg. Check: 0.55 + 1.6 = 2.15.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 3.65 = 8
items.e: Use subtraction: 8 − 3.65 = 8.00 − 3.65 = 4.35. Check: 4.35 + 3.65 = 8.00 = 8. 5.65 forgets to write the zeros: 8 − 3 = 5, then brings down .65. 11.65 adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: Zhi Hao walks 0.85 km from his HDB flat to the MRT station. Then he takes the train 6.4 km to school. How far does he travel in all?
items.e: In all means add. Line up the decimal points. Write 6.4 as 6.40. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 and rename 10 tenths as 1 one. Ones: 0 + 6 + 1 = 7. Answer: 7.25 km. Check: 7.25 − 6.4 = 0.85.

items.q: Ethan has a mass of 32.5 kg. His younger brother has a mass of 28.75 kg. How much heavier is Ethan than his brother?
items.e: How much heavier means find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 32.5 as 32.50. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs renaming. Rename 1 tenth as 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 − 7 needs renaming. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 14 − 7 = 7. Ones: 1 − 8 needs renaming. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 11 − 8 = 3. Tens: 2 − 2 = 0. Answer: 3.75 kg. Check: 3.75 + 28.75 = 32.5.

items.q: Nurul saves $15.30 in a month. Ali saves $2.85 less than Nurul. How much do they save altogether?
items.e: Step 1, Ali: $15.30 − $2.85 = $12.45. Step 2, altogether: $15.30 + $12.45 = $27.75. $12.45 is only what Ali saves. $18.15 adds $2.85 instead of taking it away. $33.45 adds $15.30, $15.30 and $2.85.

items.q: A roll of paper for a National Day banner is 5 m long. The class cuts off 1.25 m and then 2.4 m. How much paper is left?
items.e: Step 1, paper used: 1.25 m + 2.4 m = 3.65 m. Step 2, paper left: 5.00 m − 3.65 m = 1.35 m. Check: 1.35 + 3.65 = 5. 3.65 m is the paper used. 2.65 m forgets to write 5 as 5.00. 2.35 m forgets to take 1 from the ones when renaming.

items.q: Xin Yi’s water bottle holds 0.75 ℓ. Siti’s water bottle holds 1.2 ℓ. How much water do the two bottles hold altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Line up the decimal points. Write 1.2 as 1.20. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 7 + 2 = 9. Ones: 0 + 1 = 1. Answer: 1.95 ℓ. Check: 1.95 − 1.2 = 0.75.
